note: PRE-COMMITTED precursor rule-set. Rules are authored BEFORE screening, never to fit today's matches - that discipline is the entire value of this file. screen.py --precursors applies the quant_condition to produce a shortlist; the news_condition is then confirmed by a targeted sweep. Register the WHOLE match cohort in predictions.json, including unpromising matches - the non-movers are the control group. A precursor is only called 'holds up' on out-of-sample matches. See paper-trading-event-studies.md.

precursors.hypothesis: A stock carrying an unresolved regulatory or governance overhang underreacts to bullish sector news, and still underperforms VAS over the reaction window.
precursors.quant_condition: 6-month return negative AND 52-week range position below 40
precursors.quant_condition_note: UNCHANGED since registration on 2026-07-18. This was briefly tightened the same day to cut the shortlist from 37 names to 16, then REVERTED - because the change had been made after seeing which names matched, which is precisely what this file forbids, and no practical inconvenience justifies weakening that. The real problem was a conflated concern: the RULE (which must stay pre-committed) versus HOW MANY NAMES CAN BE RESEARCHED PER RUN (mere logistics). Those are now separated - see screen_budget below. SCOPE NOTE: this quant leg has NO theoretical link to governance, since an overhang is invisible in price data. It is purely an operational narrowing device; the news_condition carries all of this rule's signal.

screen_budget.note: An OPERATIONAL cap, not part of the hypothesis - it exists because a targeted news sweep over 37 names is not targeted. Applied mechanically and blind to outcomes: matches are ranked by 6-month return ascending (most beaten-down first), which is a pre-move characteristic knowable at screen time, and the top 15 are swept and registered as the cohort. Names dropped by the budget are reported in the screen output, never silently discarded. The control-group property survives because the cohort is still selected by a stated rule applied before any outcome is known, not by which names looked promising. Changing max_names or rank_by is a method change and must be logged in FINDINGS.md.

precursors.news_condition: an unresolved regulatory/governance matter disclosed in the last ~6 months (investigation, probe, restatement, board/executive conduct issue) AND identifiable bullish sector news in the last ~14 days
precursors.notes: The SHORT-WINDOW rule (30d), chosen deliberately so at least one precursor-derived prediction resolves before the ~2026-08-26 wrap rather than the track reporting as empty scaffolding. 30 days is honest here rather than convenient: the hypothesis is about the market's REACTION to a discrete news event, which is a fast process by construction - unlike the slower structural rules below. Inspired by the DRO event study, which has NOT passed a backward control test; this is the forward (Path B) test, where the non-movers in the cohort are the control.

precursors.hypothesis: On-market director buying within ~30d after a profit warning precedes outperformance vs VAS over the reaction window.
precursors.quant_condition: 52-week range position below 15 (i.e. near the 52-week low)
precursors.news_condition: a profit warning or guidance downgrade in the last ~45d AND an on-market Appendix 3Y director purchase since that warning
precursors.notes: Quant leg is screenable from yfinance; the news leg needs a targeted sweep on the shortlist. 60d because the thesis is mean-reversion after a de-rating, which is structural and slow - shortening it to beat the wrap date would misstate the hypothesis. Expect this to resolve in September, after the calibration wrap.

precursors.hypothesis: A company that has upgraded guidance more than once ahead of a scheduled result beats VAS through that result.
precursors.quant_condition: 52-week range position above 60 AND positive 6-month return
precursors.news_condition: two or more guidance upgrades in the last ~9 months AND a scheduled results date within the reaction window
precursors.notes: The obvious efficient-market objection applies with full force: repeated public upgrades are exactly the sort of thing that is already priced. Registered anyway BECAUSE it is the quant-screenable archetype - if the pre-committed expectation is right, this one should show nothing, and a null result here is a useful contrast against the news-synthesis rules.
